newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends lower but seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends lower but seen consolidating.

text.p: COMEX copper ended lower, pulled down by the LME base metals complex which took a breather to consolidate some of its recent heady gains, traders said.
LME copper stocks fell 2,450 tonnes Tuesday to 220,550 tonnes, at the low end of trader expectations. COMEX stocks on Tuesday rose 499 short tons to 24,112 tons.

"The market was overdue for a bit of consolidation," William O'Neill of Merrill Lynch said. "I would not look for too much of a setback, but maybe some further consolidation and a resumption of the uptrend."
The LME cash to three months backwardation eased also, down some $10 to $60/$64, taking away a little price support.
"But there is some anecdotal evidence that a late March to April tightness may be developing, and it's one of the things that's kept the market relatively firm here," O'Neill said.

Trading was heavy on COMEX at an estimated 23,000 lots. However, switches totaled an estimated 3,703 as the rollover from March to May continued in high gear, with the latter contract now with the most open interest.
May COMEX settled 1.05 cents weaker at 109.25 cents per pound, traded 110.50 to 108.60 cents. March went out 2.25 cents lower at 111.45 cents.
